info.name: RoomRaah API
info.description:
Every endpoint in §5 of the product document.

Start in **Auth**: run one of the "Login (seeded ...)" requests and the collection stores the access and refresh tokens for you. Then run **Locations and facilities** and **Search** once, which fill in the ids the rest of the requests use.

All seeded accounts use the password `Password1`. Emails go to Mailpit at http://localhost:8025 in development, which is where the OTP codes and the reset links are.

Live messaging is the SignalR hub at `/hubs/chat` and is not a REST request; it is described in the Messages folder.

item.name: Auth

request.description: Creates an unverified account. Rule 4: IsEmailVerified is false until the code is accepted. The OTP is emailed; in development it is visible in Mailpit at http://localhost:8025.
An owner also sends a CNIC, which §Field Validation requires of owners alone.
Returns a fresh session, because a token issued before verification is stale the moment the code is accepted. Paste the code from Mailpit.
Rule 7: at most three in any ten-minute window, answered 429 after that.
Signs in and stores both tokens on the collection, so every request below is authenticated without another step.
The owner whose identity has been checked — the only one whose listings can reach Published, per rule 23.
The admin whose CanInspect is true. admin2@roomraah.local is the one whose is false — rules 109 and 110 tell them apart.
Rule 9: the Redis revocation set first, then the database, then rotation.
Rule 10: writes a revocation entry keyed on a digest of the token, never the token itself — the cache service logs every key it touches.
Rule 12: the link works once and expires in thirty minutes.

item.description: Register, verify, sign in and out. The sign-in requests store both tokens on the collection, so everything below is authenticated.

item.name: Locations and facilities

request.description: Cities, areas and landmarks in one list. Cached for 24 hours.

item.description: Reference data, cached for 24 hours. These requests also store the ids the rest of the collection uses.

item.name: Search and public listings

request.description: Rule 29 lists every filter this accepts: cityId, areaId, landmarkId with maxDistanceKm, minRent, maxRent, roomType, genderPolicy, facilityIds, availableOnly, sort, page, pageSize.
Rule 31: the haversine runs in SQL Server, so distance sorts and pages like any other column. Rule 74: maxDistanceKm and sort=Distance both need a landmark.
Rule 82: at most eight, badge first, then the most recently confirmed availability.
Rule 35: at most three ids once duplicates are removed.
Rule 84: the owner is a display name, an identity-check verdict and the date of that check — and nothing else.
Rule 79: every photo that is not PendingAdd, and no response says which are pending.
Rule 94: Approved only, newest first, with the average and the count.

item.description: Anonymous. Browsing is public; acting requires an account.

request.description: Rule 34: once per person. Rule 86: only a published listing.
Rule 87: newest save first, and only the listings still published.
Rule 87: a save whose listing left the site is kept and stays deletable.

item.name: Visits

request.description: Rule 36: one open request per listing per seeker. Rule 92: the owner is emailed.
Rule 93: the seeker is named by display name alone, and the owner not at all.
Rule 88: only from Requested. Rule 89: a decline requires the note.
Rule 90: only from Accepted, only once the preferred time has passed, by either party. §5 named no endpoint for this, which left rule 38 gating a feature nothing could reach.
Rule 91: the seeker who made it, from Requested or Accepted only.

item.description: The only way a visit is arranged in this product — there are no call buttons and no WhatsApp links anywhere in it.

request.description: Rule 38: only after a visit on this listing reached Completed. Rule 41: it is created Pending and is invisible until an admin approves it.
Rule 42: one unresolved report per listing per person, where unresolved means Open or UnderReview.

item.name: Messages

request.description: Rule 43 made a conversation unique per property and seeker, and §5 named no endpoint that opened one. Calling this twice returns the existing thread with 200 rather than refusing.
Rule 101: most recent message first, and the other participant by display name alone.
Oldest first, which is the order a conversation is read in.
Rule 105: pushed over /hubs/chat while the recipient is connected, and emailed when they are not — at most one email per conversation per recipient per hour.
Rule 104: marks everything the caller did not send, and answers with how many. A thread with nothing unread marks nothing and is not a refusal.

item.description: What §Contact Stays On the Site promises instead of a phone number. Live delivery is the SignalR hub at {{baseUrl}}/../hubs/chat, which Postman cannot drive — the token goes in the access_token query parameter because a WebSocket handshake cannot set a header.

item.name: Owner listings

request.description: Rule 14: created as Draft. Rule 17: latitude and longitude are required — the owner drops a pin, there is no geocoder in this product.

request.description: Rule 18: an owner reads and modifies only their own.
§9: 5 MB maximum, jpeg/png/webp checked by decoding the bytes rather than by the extension. Every upload generates a thumbnail.

formdata.description: A jpeg, png or webp under 5 MB.

request.description: The list must name every photo the listing will hold, exactly once.
Exactly one per listing; it is what a card shows.
Rule 54: in place while the listing is not Published, and a proposal once it is.
Rule 52: only from Draft or ChangesRequested. Rule 15: between three and fifteen live photographs.
Rule 19: editing a Published listing creates a revision. The live row is never modified by an owner.

request.description: Rule 21: a bed count on its own lands in the availability queue rather than the content one. Re-confirming an unchanged count is accepted here and refused on PUT — it is what keeps the listing off the stale list.
Rule 108: once per listing. After the first visit RoomRaah re-inspects on its own schedule, and no response anywhere names a date that has not happened.

item.description: Sign in as the owner first. Rule 19: once a listing is published, an edit becomes a revision rather than a write.

item.name: Admin - listings and revisions

request.description: Oldest submission first. Nothing in the admin area is cached.
The verification checks and an owner summary — with no phone number and no email address, because rule 33 has no exception for an admin panel.
Rule 23: OwnerIdentity, Address, Photos and Facilities must all pass before a listing can be published. Availability is recordable but does not gate publishing.
Rule 24: sets Published and stamps AvailabilityConfirmedAt. Rule 124: this is also the way an Unpublished listing comes back.
Rule 26: a refusal requires a note, or the owner has nothing to act on.
Rule 122: only from Published, and only with a note. §5 had ten admin listing endpoints and none of them set this status, so a listing could never leave the public site through the API.
Two queues, because availability is not a price change. Pass kind=Availability for the other one.
The before-and-after an admin decides from.
Rule 25: copies the fields onto the listing, applies the pending photo transitions and drops the properties: cache prefix.
Rule 27: the live listing is left exactly as it was.

item.description: Sign in as an admin first.

request.description: Rule 41 created every review Pending and §5 had no endpoint that moved one, which left the public review list empty for the life of the product.
Rule 96: Approved or Hidden, and either may be set from either of the other two.
Rule 97: UnderReview, Upheld or Dismissed; the two verdicts require a note and cannot be set twice. Rule 98: upholding does not take the listing down.

item.name: Admin - inspections and the badge

request.description: Rule 109: only an admin whose CanInspect is true, and only against a date that has already passed — a future date would be a scheduled visit, which rule 115 says does not exist anywhere in this product.

body.raw:
{
  "propertyId": "{{propertyId}}",
  "inspectedAt": "2026-09-01T11:00:00Z",
  "result": "Passed",
  "notes": "Rooms, facilities and the address all matched the listing.",
  "feeAmount": 1500,
  "feeCollectedAt": "2026-08-31T09:00:00Z"
}

request.description: Rule 114: badged listings not visited in thirty days, longest overdue first. A query rather than a sweep — a WHERE clause is right without having had to run.
Rule 110: only when the most recent inspection passed, only by an admin who makes visits, and never twice. Rule 112: the reason is required and is recorded.
Rule 111: any admin. A claim being withdrawn must not wait for the one person who makes visits.

item.description: The only paid feature in the product. Sign in as admin@roomraah.local, whose CanInspect is true; admin2@roomraah.local is the one it is false for.

item.name: Admin - users

request.description: Rule 117: every account including the deactivated ones — leave isActive off to see them. This list carries no CNIC and no phone number.

Rule 116: the only endpoint in the product that returns a phone number, and the only one that returns a CNIC. It exists so that the admin recording the OwnerIdentity check can see the identity being checked.
Rule 118: not your own account, and not another admin. Rule 11: a deactivated account cannot log in.
§5 listed only the deactivation, which made a misclick permanent.

item.description: The one area of §5 that belonged to no phase of the build plan.
